claims.claim: Name badge canonical solution is an on-start block running showString("NAME") once to scroll the name; the correct structure is event-driven single-run, NOT a forever loop, which would re-scroll constantly.

Beating heart canonical solution uses a forever loop alternating showIcon(Heart) and showIcon(SmallHeart) with pause blocks between frames; placing the animation in on-start is a key mistake because it runs only once and shows no beating.
Beating heart answer keys must require pause blocks (e.g., 500ms) between the two heart frames; omitting pauses is a common kid mistake that makes the icon flicker too fast to perceive as 'beating'.

Emotion badge canonical solution uses on-button-pressed (A, B) and on-gesture-shake event handlers each showing one icon; the answer key should flag forever-loop polling with if/else as a non-canonical, less responsive structure.

Step counter canonical solution initializes a counter variable to 0 on start, increments it on shake, and shows the number on button A; answer keys must flag missing initialization (NaN/junk display) and using a button press instead of the shake gesture.

Nightlight canonical solution is a forever loop with an if comparing input.lightLevel() BELOW a threshold to light LEDs and an else to clear them; common mistakes are reversing the comparison (>) or using equality (=) instead of a threshold range.

Across all short MakeCode tasks the canonical structure is event-driven blocks (on start / on button / on gesture) plus a forever loop only where repetition is needed; answer keys should flag non-canonical control flow such as showString inside forever or missing clear/reset steps.
